name: Iberian Vernacular

description.short: The whitewashed courtyard house of southern Spain — thick walls, small openings, deep shade, and a patio that does the work of a room.
description.long:
The Andalusian house is the Islamic courtyard diagram sustained in ordinary building for a thousand years: a blank whitewashed street wall, a controlled entry, and an interior court planted and often fitted with water. The climate logic is exact — thermal mass, night flushing, shaded transitional space, minimized solar gain on the envelope.

This is the most technically relevant traditional inheritance available for the American Sun Belt, and it is almost entirely unexploited by production builders there, who instead build Midwestern houses with more insulation.

defining_characteristics: Blank whitewashed street elevation and one controlled entry
Interior patio as the principal living space for much of the year
Very thick lime-rendered masonry with deep reveals
Small high openings and generous shaded galleries
Water and planting as architectural rather than decorative elements

exemplars.name: Palacio de Viana
exemplars.why: Derived, not authored: `andalusian-courtyard-vernacular`, a style of this family, names it its icon, and the reason for that judgment is recorded on that node rather than restated here.

sources: Luis Feduchi, Itinerarios de arquitectura popular espanola, IV: Los pueblos blancos (1978)
Fernando Garcia Mercadal, La casa popular en Espana (1930)
